summary: 文章追溯侦探小说如何从坡的创作走向英国，经福尔摩斯和两次世界大战之间的黄金时代而风靡一时。随着阶层秩序和公众对理性、司法公正的信念改变，经典解谜模式逐渐衰落。
logic: 福尔摩斯确立名侦探形象
黄金时代呈现阶层惯例与偏见
对照美国硬汉派的发展
社会信念转变伴随经典形式衰落

paragraphs.brief: 侦探故事从美法移植到英国
sentences: The detective story is normally said to have begun in the fertile brain of the great American writer Edgar Allan Poe (1809–49), especially in his stories featuring the detective C. Auguste Dupin.
侦探故事通常被追溯到美国作家埃德加·爱伦·坡（1809—1849）的丰富想象，尤其是他以侦探奥古斯特·杜宾为主角的作品。
From 1859, Dupin had a counterpart in Monsieur Lecoq, created by the French author Emile Gaboriau.
从1859年起，杜宾在法国有了同行，即埃米尔·加博里奥笔下的勒科克先生。
Despite these American and French origins, it was to Britain that detective fiction migrated, where it took root and flourished, becoming a characteristically British genre.
尽管有这些美国和法国血统，侦探小说还是迁移到英国，在那里，它生根和繁荣，成为一个典型的英国风格。
paragraphs.gist: 侦探故事常被追溯到美国作家坡笔下的杜宾和法国的勒科克，后来却在英国扎根兴盛，发展为带有鲜明英国色彩的类型。

paragraphs.brief: 福尔摩斯形象与真实警方的反差
sentences: This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective.
这一转变是因为一位作家和他的伟大的侦探。

The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories.
阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士于1887年首次出版《血字的研究》，让最著名的虚构侦探夏洛克·福尔摩斯初次登场；后来他成为四部长篇和五十六篇短篇的主角。
Nearly all of the Holmes stories are narrated by his friend Dr Watson.
几乎所有福尔摩斯的故事都由他的朋友华生医生讲述
Watson is constantly amazed and stupefied by Holmes’s genius, but despite years of working with him, Watson is never able to produce these brilliant insights himself.
华生每每被福尔摩斯的天才惊得目瞪口呆，尽管与他合作多年，却始终无法自己作出同样精彩的推断。
Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits.
福尔摩斯古怪得令人难忘，各种习惯有些讨喜，有些则没那么可爱。
He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled.
这位出色的私家侦探远胜苏格兰场那些迟钝平庸的官员，而他们每遇棘手案件就来找他。

This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.
这种情景完全是虚构的：现实中苏格兰场破案受挫时并没有什么神探可求助，而其刑事调查部门其实十分能干，破案率也很高。
paragraphs.gist: 柯南·道尔笔下，华生总为福尔摩斯的独到推理折服，苏格兰场也常向他求助；现实中的警方其实能力很强，鲜少需要这种虚构救星。

paragraphs.brief: 小说中的上流社会与现实犯罪
sentences: Most of the Holmes stories are set among the higher levels of 19th-century British society, a world inhabited by professional men, retired army officers and country gentlemen, as well as members of royalty and cabinet ministers.
福尔摩斯故事多以十九世纪英国上层社会为背景，人物包括专业人士、退役军官、乡绅，也有王室成员和内阁大臣。
Few take place among the working classes or the very poor, whereas in fact much crime was a product of the poverty and gangs in London’s underworld.
故事很少发生在工人阶层或赤贫人群之中，尽管现实中许多犯罪恰与伦敦地下社会的贫穷和帮派有关。
paragraphs.gist: 福尔摩斯案件多发生在专业人士、乡绅和政要的圈子里，很少涉及工人或穷人，与当时伦敦地下社会中贫困、帮派引发的犯罪并不相称。

paragraphs.brief: 黄金时代的理性信念和社会偏见
sentences: In the 20th century detective stories became increasingly popular.
在20世纪侦探故事越来越流行。
Reading these stories was one of the characteristic aspects of the British middle classes in the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction—the 1920s and 30s.
阅读这些故事是1920年代和30年代英国侦探小说 " 黄金时代 " 英国中产阶级的特点之一。
Their emphasis on rationality, the inevitable triumph of justice, and the existence of an unofficial super-detective tells us much about the society of the time.
他们强调理性、正义不可避免的胜利以及非官方超级侦探的存在，这使我们对当时的社会非常了解。

So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner.
作品的定型角色和隐含偏见也反映社会风貌：乡下人和家仆几乎总被写得愚笨，女性常被简单扁平化，只有少数女作家把女性写得更真实。
paragraphs.gist: 二十世纪二三十年代的中产读者喜爱理性终将伸张正义的故事，但小说对乡民、仆役和女性的刻板描写也折射了当时的偏见。

paragraphs.brief: 作家的中产出身与有限报酬
sentences: Most of the well-known British authors of ‘golden age’ detective stories were drawn from the middle classes, like their audience.
英国知名的"黄金时代"侦探故事作者大多来自中产阶级就像他们的观众一样

Conan Doyle was a doctor who turned to writing fiction while he awaited his patients; Freeman Wills Crofts was a railway engineer in Northern Ireland; Gilbert Keith Chesterton and Anthony Berkeley were journalists; Cecil Street a career army officer.
科南·多伊尔是一位医生，在等待病人时转而写小说；弗里曼·威尔斯·克罗夫茨是北爱尔兰的铁路工程师；吉尔伯特·基思·切斯特顿和安东尼·伯克利是记者；塞西尔·斯特尔是职业军官。
Apart from a few superstars such as Agatha Christie, financial rewards for these interwar authors were rather meagre; a few hundred pounds per book—a useful income, but nothing princely.
两次世界大战之间，除阿加莎·克里斯蒂等少数明星作家外，多数作者每本书只挣几百英镑；这笔收入有所补益，却算不上丰厚。
paragraphs.gist: 黄金时代的作家多与读者一样出自中产阶层，白天可能是医生、工程师或记者；除克里斯蒂等明星外，一本书通常只赚几百英镑。

paragraphs.brief: 美国硬汉派借侦探故事批判社会
sentences: US writers such as Rex Stout and Ellery Queen attempted to recreate the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction.
美国作家，如Rex Stout和Ellery Queen试图重新创造英国侦探小说的 " 金时代 "。
For the most part their books were mere imitations of the British models, although they were seldom wholly successful.
他们的书大多只是模仿英国的模型，尽管很少完全成功。
But in the 1920s and 1930s, America also saw the rise of the ‘hard-boiled’ genre and its detective type: the tough private cop who appeared in the works of Dashiell Hammett and Raymond Chandler.
不过在二十世纪二三十年代，美国也兴起了「硬汉派」及其标志性侦探，即哈米特和钱德勒作品中作风强硬的私家侦探。

Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life.
除了在整个作品中出现的暴力外，Hammett和Chandler的小说常常带有政治色彩，试图揭露他们所看到的处于美国生活核心的不平等。

Britain had no real parallel either to their outlook on the world or (until much later) to their violence, but upheld the belief that the authorities should punish criminals regardless of their circumstances.
当时英国作品中没有真正相似的世界观，也要到很晚才有相当的暴力描写；英国作家仍相信不论有什么背景，当局都应惩罚罪犯。
paragraphs.gist: 美国除模仿英国黄金时代，也发展出哈米特与钱德勒的硬汉派，借暴力情节和强悍私探揭露不平等，与英国传统的正义观拉开距离。

paragraphs.brief: 旧式谜题让位于警察和情节转折
sentences: By around 1960, the classic British detective story was in serious decline.
约到1960年，经典英国侦探故事已明显衰落。
It seemed that writers had simply run out of ingenious plots and puzzles for their detectives to solve.
作家们似乎已想不出更多精巧的情节与谜题供侦探破解。
The best-known crime fiction writers, such as P. D. James, eschewed private detectives for police inspectors, and straightforward puzzles for stories that were full of unexpected twists.
P. D. 詹姆斯等知名犯罪小说家放下私家侦探，改写警察督察，也用转折出人意料的故事取代单纯的解谜。
paragraphs.gist: 到 1960 年前后经典英国侦探故事渐趋衰落，新作转而让警察督察办案，用出人意料的转折取代单纯的智力谜题。

paragraphs.brief: 侦探小说衰落折射社会信念改变
sentences: Today the detective story no longer exists in Britain, at least in its old form.
今天，侦探的故事不再存在于英国，至少以它的旧形式。
Arguably this mirrors the transformation of that society as a whole.
可以说，这反映了整个社会的转变。

The belief that scientific developments were invariably beneficial possibly reached its height during the period when the classic detective story flourished, as did the belief in putting rationality at the heart of Britain’s education system.
在经典侦探小说的鼎盛时期，英国社会对科学进步必有益处的信念或许也达到顶峰，坚持把理性放在教育核心的想法同样如此。

And finally, the central belief that evil-doers would inevitably get their just deserts through the incorruptibility of the judicial system was replaced by a questioning of some of the procedures and decisions associated with that system.
最后，曾经的核心信念是司法清正、作恶者终将受到应得惩罚；后来，人们却开始质疑司法体系的某些程序与裁决。
paragraphs.gist: 旧式侦探故事退场也折射英国社会观念的转变：人们对科学进步、理性教育和司法必能惩恶的信念，都不再像从前那样笃定。

items.en: C. Auguste Dupin and Émile Gaboriau were both writers of detective stories.
items.zh: 奥古斯特·杜宾和埃米尔·加博里奥都是侦探小说作家。
items.why: Dupin是侦探角色而非作者。Gaboriau才是作者。题干称“两人都是侦探小说作家”,与原文不符。

items.en: It was Conan Doyle’s creation of Sherlock Holmes that made the detective story a typically British genre.
items.zh: 柯南·道尔创造了夏洛克·福尔摩斯，使侦探小说成为具有典型英国特色的体裁。
items.why: 原文把“转变为英国体裁”的原因明确归因于柯南道尔创造的福尔摩斯，与题干一致。

items.en: The positive qualities of the character of Sherlock Holmes outweigh the negative qualities.
items.zh: 福尔摩斯性格上的优点多于缺点。
items.why: 文中只罗列正负特质，并未比较“正面是否多于负面/outweigh”。无此信息，选NG。

items.en: Officials at Scotland Yard were unhappy at the way they were portrayed in the Sherlock Holmes stories.
items.zh: 伦敦警察厅的官员不满自己在福尔摩斯故事中的形象。
items.why: 这里说明现实与小说不符，但没有提到苏格兰场官员是否“不满”被描写方式，信息缺失。

items.en: Sherlock Holmes is based on a real private detective who was consulted by Scotland Yard.
items.zh: 福尔摩斯的原型是一名曾受伦敦警察厅咨询的真实私家侦探。
items.why: 作者说苏格兰场遇到破不了的案子时求助天才私家侦探纯属虚构，因此没有题干所指的现实原型。

items.en: Conan Doyle’s work fails to reflect the reality of crime in 19th-century Britain.
items.zh: 柯南·道尔的作品未能反映 19 世纪英国犯罪的实际情况。
items.why: 小说主要写上层社会，未反映当时犯罪多源于贫困与黑帮的现实，因此“fails to reflect the reality”成立。

items.en: In the 1920s and 1930s, most writers of detective stories started to include interesting female characters in their work.
items.zh: 20 世纪二三十年代，大多数侦探小说作家开始在作品中加入引人入胜的女性角色。
items.why: 1920s-30s的大多数作家仍把女性写得扁平。只有“少数女作家”更真实。与“most writers…interesting female characters” 相反。

items.en: Agatha Christie only earned a few hundred pounds for her books.
items.zh: 阿加莎·克里斯蒂靠出书只赚了几百英镑。
items.why: “几百英镑/本”是大多数人的酬劳。阿加莎属于“少数超级明星”,显然不止如此。题干说她“只有几百英镑*,与文意相反。

items.en: In the USA in the 1920s–1930s, Rex Stout and Ellery Queen’s works were mainly unsuccessful ________ of British detective fiction.
items.zh: 20世纪二三十年代的美国，雷克斯·斯托特与埃勒里·奎因的作品大多是对英国侦探小说不太成功的________。
items.why: Ri: Rex Stout 和 Ellery Queen 的作品“主要是不成功的英国侦探小说”。对应词为 imitations (模仿/仿作)。

items.en: The works of Hammett and Chandler were full of ________.
items.zh: 哈米特和钱德勒的作品充斥着________。
items.why: “were full of ”对应整段指出其作品“遍布暴力”。

items.en: Hammett and Chandler’s works had a ________ message about the unfairness of society.
items.zh: 哈米特和钱德勒的作品借社会不公传递了带有________色彩的信息。
items.why: 题干“had a message about the unfairness of society”= 具有关于社会不公的政治信息/诉求，取 political。

items.en: In 1950s–1960s Britain, writers such as P. D. James created stories with many ________.
items.zh: 20世纪五六十年代的英国，P. D. 詹姆斯等作家创作的故事往往包含多处情节________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“P. D. 詹姆斯等知名犯罪小说家放下私家侦探，改写警察督察，也用转折出人意料的故事取代单纯的解谜”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: In present-day Britain, scientific progress is not always seen as ________.
items.zh: 在当代英国，人们并非总认为科学进步是________的。
items.why: 现在的社会变化意味着科学进步并非总被视为“beneficial”,故填 beneficial。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 两个副词都描述这种文学体裁带有典型的英国特点。
the inequality they saw at the heart of American life
原文具体指作家看到的美国社会不平等，对应题干概括的社会不公。
第 3 段 · 第 1 句
第 8 段 · 第 2 句
points: “几百英镑/本”是大多数人的酬劳。阿加莎属于“少数超级明星”,显然不止如此。题干说她“只有几百英镑*,与文意相反。
“were full of ”对应整段指出其作品“遍布暴力”。
clauses: This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives …, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.
“to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed”修饰前面的 detectives。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 whom 时，回看 detectives，再把修饰信息接回主句。

So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, ….
连接词 although 引出“although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Detective stories became hugely popular in the 19th and 20th centuries.
侦探故事在19世纪和20世纪变得非常流行。
William D. Rubinstein looks at why social changes eventually led to their downfall.
威廉·鲁宾斯坦探讨了社会变迁为何最终导致侦探小说式微。
